prior_counterpart_excerpt: Note that because safeguards such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) or constitutional training can almost certainly be fine-tuned away within the specified 1% of training cost, and also because the ASL-3 standard applies if the model is dangerous at any stage in its training (for example after pretraining but before RLHF), fine-tuning-based safeguards are likely irrelevant to whether a model qualifies as ASL-3.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Evaluation science is not yet mature enough to confidently set a precise buffer to a Capability Threshold, though this remains an aspiration.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: We mitigate this risk by creating a buffer: we have intentionally designed our ASL evaluations to trigger at slightly lower capability levels than those we are concerned about, while ensuring we evaluate at defined, regular intervals (specifically every 4x increase in effective compute, as defined below) in order to limit the amount of overshoot that is possible.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models

prior_counterpart_excerpt: By “non-state attackers” we mean both persistent and opportunistic non-state attackers. This category includes hacker groups, terrorist groups, and industrial espionage but we exclude a small number (~10) of non-state actors with state-level resourcing or backing.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard was updated to allow safeguard levels to vary by deployment context.
prior_counterpart_excerpt: Tiered access: In limited cases, models with capabilities relevant to catastrophic harm may be made available to a select group of vetted users with a legitimate and beneficial use-case that cannot be separated from dangerous capabilities, and only if such access can be granted safely and with sufficient oversight.

locator: Changelog / Oct 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
